cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Religion & Culture
cards.back: The Greeks worshipped the twelve Olympian gods, each with specific domains: Zeus (king of gods), Hera (marriage), Athena (wisdom), Apollo (prophecy/music), Poseidon (sea), Ares (war), Aphrodite (love), etc.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Religion & Culture
cards.back: Sacrifice (thusia) was the central act of Greek worship: animal sacrifices were offered at temples and altars, with the gods receiving the bones and fat while worshippers ate the meat

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Religion & Culture
cards.back: Oracles, especially Delphi (sacred to Apollo), provided divine guidance on major decisions: war, colonisation, politics

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Religion & Culture
cards.back: Pan-Hellenic festivals (Olympic, Pythian, Nemean, Isthmian Games) brought Greeks together in celebration and athletic competition

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Religion & Culture
cards.back: Hubris (arrogance against the gods) and miasma (ritual pollution from murder) were serious religious concerns

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Religion & Culture
cards.back: Religion was embedded in every aspect of life: no separation between religion and state; priests were state officials

cards.front: What should you know about gcse ancient history exam tips — greek religion & culture?
cards.back: 1. For Greek Religion & Culture, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2.
